 Economy 
 November 2 — deadline for filing income tax returns in Armenia: What you need to know
 02.11.2026, 
 10:22 
 Monday, November 2, marks the deadline for filing annual personal income tax returns for 2025 in Armenia. 
 YEREVAN, November 2. /ARKA/. Monday, November 2, marks the deadline for filing annual personal income tax returns for 2025 in Armenia. The State Revenue Committee (SRC) reminds you who is required to file a tax return, how to verify the information, and what income must be declared.
 The deadline was initially set for November 1, 2026. However, since this date falls on a non-working day, in accordance with the Law "On Regulatory Legal Acts," the deadline has been extended to the next working day, November 2.
 Who is required to file a tax return
 The obligation to declare income for 2025 applies to individuals who simultaneously meet the following conditions:
 - are tax residents of the Republic of Armenia;
 - were citizens of Armenia as of December 31, 2025;
 - have reached the age of majority by the specified date.
 Therefore, the 2025 tax declaration system covers adult citizens of Armenia who are tax residents of the country.
 How to file a tax declaration
 The State Revenue Committee pre-populates tax declarations based on information available in the tax authority's information system.
 To independently submit a tax declaration, you must verify your identity, activate your electronic signature, and log in to the State Revenue Committee's Unified System of Electronic Services for Individuals.
 After logging in, you must review the pre-populated information, make any changes or additions necessary, certify the tax declaration with an electronic signature, and submit it.
 The tax declaration can also be submitted through an authorized representative. Notarization of the power of attorney is not required.
 What income is exempt from declaration?
 For the 2025 reporting year, a simplified procedure for declaring certain types of non-taxable income is provided.
 In particular, certain income received as a result of gifts, loans from other individuals, alienation of property, or gratuitous receipt of property may not need to be reported, provided the value of each individual transaction does not exceed 1 million drams.
 If the value of an individual transaction exceeds the established threshold, the corresponding income must be declared in full.
 Furthermore, non-taxable income received from family members, including spouses, parents, siblings, children, grandparents, and grandchildren, is not subject to declaration, regardless of the amount. This rule also applies to relationships between adoptive parents and adopted children.
 What income must be reported?
 If a citizen received taxable income during 2025, including from real estate rentals, from foreign countries or other sources, it must be reflected in the annual tax return in cases provided by law.
 When receiving income from a tax agent, the tax agent is responsible for calculating, withholding, and transferring income tax to the budget.
 If the income was not received through a tax agent, such as from another individual or a foreign organization, the citizen must independently calculate and pay the tax in cases established by law.
 What happens if a tax return is not filed by November 2?
 According to the State Revenue Committee, if a citizen fails to submit a tax return by the deadline, the tax return pre-filled by the tax authority is automatically considered filed after the deadline.
 However, the citizen retains the ability to subsequently amend the tax return.
 The Committee recommends verifying the completeness and accuracy of the information, as a pre-filled tax return may require supplementation.
 How to receive reimbursement for social expenses
 Citizens eligible for reimbursement for social expenses for education and healthcare must submit a tax return certified with an electronic signature.
 After this, a separate application for reimbursement must be submitted through the same electronic system.
 Compensation may be provided for eligible expenses of both the individual and their family members—spouse, parents, and children.
 When will income declarations for 2026 be due?
 Income declarations for the 2026 reporting year will begin on March 2, 2027. The deadline for filing declarations is July 1, 2027.
 Additional information on the declaration procedure and necessary steps is available in the "Declarations" section on the official website of the State Revenue Committee of Armenia.
